Subject: PO requirements + split invoicing request

Hi Neha,

Quick one from our procurement side as we prepare the PO for Redwood. Our legal/finance team requires:
- Company PO referencing both Clearline account code (CL-4182) and SKU tags at the line-item level.
- Net60 on invoices (internal policy).
- Ability to split the contract into an upfront deposit + monthly consumption invoices (they asked for 30% upfront, remainder invoiced monthly).
- We attach our standard PO template for your finance team.

Two questions before I draft the PO:
1) Would Redwood apply any committed-spend or prepay discount tied to the upfront deposit?
2) Can you confirm whether discounts would flow to overage/usage lines or only to the committed base?

Can we hop on a short call tomorrow to lock this down? Thanks — Cameron

Attachments: Clearline_PO_Template.xlsx

Cameron Price

Subject: Re: PO requirements + split invoicing request

Hi Cameron — thanks for the clear list, and for sending the template. Appreciate the heads-up on the net60 requirement.

Short answers up front:
- We can support a 30% upfront deposit + monthly invoices for consumption.
- We can also include PO and SKU tags on each invoice line (finance can mirror the line-item mapping you include in the PO).
- Discounts: we typically tie prepay/commit discounts to committed spend (the amount covered by the PO/commit). Overages are billed at standard list rates unless otherwise agreed; we can discuss a reduced overage multiplier if needed.

Suggested commercial framework for clarity and to keep your approvers happy:
- Option A (standard): 30% upfront prepayment at signing + monthly invoices for consumption. Committed spend covered by the PO receives a 7% discount off list. Overages billed at list price.
- Option B (deeper discount for larger prepay): 50% upfront prepayment at signing + monthly invoices = 10% discount on committed spend.
- In both options we will mark invoices with the PO number and SKU tags per your template.

Operational note: Redwood prefers net30 on invoice payment terms when we issue monthly invoices, but given enterprise cadence we can accept net60 as long as the upfront prepay clears at signing. If net60 is a hard finance constraint on all invoices, we should map that in the SOW and consider a one-time onboarding credit to adjust unit economics.

I attached a one-page reply template to show how we’d map line items back to your PO (Redwood_PO_Reply_Template.xlsx). I’ve cc’d Vanessa (finance) and Karthik (legal) so they can weigh in on invoicing and PO acceptance.

If you’re free tomorrow at 10:00 PT I can hop on a quick call to finalize.

Best,
Neha Kapoor

Redwood Inference

On Fri, Jul 11, 2025 at 11:03 AM Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Short answers up front:
> - We can support a 30% upfront deposit + monthly invoices for consumption.
> - We can also include PO and SKU tags on each invoice line...

Thanks Neha — that helps. A few clarifications from procurement:
- Net60 is our default for all vendors; having upfront prepay is the only way we can speed approvals. We can likely get the 30% prepay approved quickly.
- Regarding overages: procurement is sensitive to unpredictability. If overages are billed at list and we incur a large burst month we may struggle to reconcile. Would Redwood consider applying the same discount band to overages in the first 12 months (or at least cap the overage rate to 120% of list)?
- For the SKU tags: they ask that SKU codes appear in the PO and be repeated on every invoice line — this is non-negotiable for their AP system.

If we can confirm those three points we’ll prepare the PO this afternoon. Can you confirm whether the discount applies to credits/committed seats or to total invoice line dollars? Also can you share the SOW you mentioned?

Thanks — Cameron
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jul 2025 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO requirements + split invoicing request

Hi Cameron — great questions. Getting practical:
1) Overages and caps: We can apply the committed-spend discount to the committed PO amount only. For overages, we will bill at list price but agree to cap the effective overage billing at 120% of list for the first 12 months post-activation. That gives you predictability while protecting Redwood unit economics.
2) Discount scope: Discounts will apply to invoice dollars attributable to committed SKU lines (the line items mapped to the PO/commit). If you expect unpredictable variable usage you can increase the committed band to have those lines covered under the discount.
3) SKU tagging & PO fields: We will stamp every invoice line with your SKU code and PO number exactly as provided, and match the invoice CSV to your template for automated ingestion. Vanessa will coordinate the exact field mapping with your AP contact.
4) Payment terms: To accommodate Clearline’s net60 policy we propose: upfront 30% prepay (due at signing) + monthly invoices for usage that are payable net30 from invoice date. Practically this gives Clearline the internal approval comfort while keeping most invoices on a shorter term. If procurement requires net60 on every invoice we can accept that as a concession but would request a one-time onboarding credit of 3% to offset extended DSO on the recurring portion.

Next steps:
- I’m attaching SOW_v2.pdf with the commit band and SKU mapping examples.
- Vanessa will reach out (cc’d) to set a 30-minute mapping call to confirm invoice CSV columns and finalize PO field mappings.
- If that works, you can send the PO this afternoon and we’ll turn on the contract onboarding flows.

Proposed meeting window: Mon 14 Jul between 09:00–11:00 PT — Vanessa, does that work for you?

Thanks — looking forward to closing it out.
